title: Retention watermarking and proof-of-eviction for prompts and metrics
creator: Priya Shah
description: Implement a lightweight retention 'watermark' mechanism and compact proof-of-eviction artifacts for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics. The goal is to enable reproducible evidence that a given artifact was retained until policy expiry and then deterministically removed without maintaining bulky full-history exports. This will support compliance audits and reduce storage/evidence export costs.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime writes a per-request retention watermark entry at creation time containing a stable, compact fingerprint and TTL metadata
Eviction process produces an append-only, signed proof-of-eviction bundle containing hashes and timestamps that auditors can verify against stored watermarks
Watermarking and proof generation add <5% p95 tail latency overhead on steady-state serving in benchmarked workloads
Evidence bundles can be exported on-demand for a tenant, filtered by route and time range, and verified independently using documented verification steps
Security review completed and HSM/KMS signing integrated for proof attestation where customer requires key separation
technical_notes: Design uses two compact artifacts per request: (1) a content fingerprint (BLAKE3) with deterministic canonicalization for prompts/responses/structured logs and (2) a small TTL manifest stored in retention-index (sharded by tenant). Eviction will move TTL manifests into an immutable eviction-log with batch-signed Merkle roots to compress proofs. We will leverage existing runtime hooks (ENG-51234) to emit watermarks at request finalize and reuse the KV-cache batching window to amortize hashing cost. Trade-offs: signing every request increases operational cost; we batch-sign Merkle roots to balance auditability and cost. We'll surface verification tooling (CLI + Console) that reproduces hashes given the original artifact and verifies inclusion/exclusion in the eviction-log.
updates: 2025-02-18: Ticket created after spike showing feasibility of compact Merkle proofs for eviction chains. Priya authored initial spec.

2025-02-24: Architecture sync w/ runtime and storage teams. Agreed to use BLAKE3 canonicalization; storage will add retention-index shard for watermarks. Action: ENG storage to prototype index schema (ENG-33782).
2025-02-28: Prototype bench results: single-request fingerprint cost ~0.7ms on p50, 1.8ms p95 under 4096 token artifact; within overhead target. Need to ensure CPU budgeting on tail-heavy workloads.

2025-03-02: Design review with Security and Compliance. Security requested KMS/HSM-backed signing for tenant-level proofs and retention of signing keys for 90 days for auditability. Added security checklist and gating item.

2025-03-04: Implementation started: added watermark emitter to request finalizer hook; retention-index write path implemented. Opened PR runtime#2765. Noted conflict with autoscaling path for dedicated instances — added fallback to async emitter when under memory pressure.

2025-03-06: PR feedback from runtime reviewers: adjust batching window and add backpressure metrics. QA to create synthetic auditor that validates proof bundles end-to-end. Planned follow-up: spike on signing throughput and HSM cost estimates.
Follow-ups: add Console export UI, document verification CLI, affordability analysis for tenant-level HSM signing, integration test for cross-region eviction proofs.
